title: Metric Sentinel Design & Adaptive Throttle Notes (WIP)
content:
Context:

This note collects design ideas and oncall procedures for a "metric sentinel" layer that sits in front of our alerting stack. Goal: reduce wasted pages from transient metric gaps and signal spikes, while preserving high-fidelity SLO burn alerts. This is intentionally experimental — recording heuristics, example queries, and a minimal oncall triage flow we can test on a small set of services first.

Motivation / observed problems:
- Frequent pages caused by upstream instrumentation gaps (short-lived exporter crashes, scrape latency spikes).
- Certain downstream SLOs trigger chaff alerts while root-cause metrics (e.g., GPU utilization, request queue depth) remain stable.
- Current static thresholds don't account for diurnal traffic or release-day variance.
- Oncall time is dominated by chasing whether an incident is real vs telemetry artifact.

High-level approach (sentinel concepts):
1) Synthetics-first sentinel: run lightweight synthetic probes (latency check, lightweight inference echo) for critical paths. If synthetic is green, demote noisy metric-based alerts to informational.

2) Multi-evaluator scoring: each incoming candidate alert is evaluated by a small set of validators (metric continuity, scrape health, correlated signals, historical z-score). Validators output a confidence band; sum yields an alert score used to route or throttle.

3) Adaptive throttle / circuit-breaker: for a given rule group, automatically apply a short backoff when many low-confidence alerts occur in a short window. Backoff parameters are service-scoped and bounded by SLO urgency.

4) Fast-fail for SLO burn: any strong SLO burn signal (error budget depletion > configured ramp) escapes throttles and pages at high priority.

Validator heuristics (examples):
- scrape_ok_ratio: proportion of successful scrapes in last 15m for exporters tied to metric. If < 90% -> lower confidence.
- contiguous_samples: number of contiguous non-NaN samples in last N points. Short runs -> suspect instrumentation gap.
- historical_delta_z: how far current value deviates from same-day-of-week baseline (rolling 30d). Use robust MAD-based z-score.
- cross-metric-corroboration: e.g., request latency spike should align with increased request_count or backend CPU/queue_depth. Absent corroboration reduces confidence.

Example PromQL snippets (to be validated in staging):
- scrape_ok_ratio: sum_over_time(up{job=~"exporter-.*"}[15m]) / (15 * 60)  # rough placeholder
- contiguous_samples: count_over_time((metric_name != NaN)[5m:30s]) # verify PromQL semantics before use

Alert scoring model (simple start):
- score = 100 (base)
- -30 if scrape_ok_ratio < 0.9
- -25 if contiguous_samples < threshold_for_metric
- -20 if no corroborating metric change in 5m window
- +50 if matched synthetic probe failure
- +40 if error_budget_depletion_rate > high_cutoff

Routing decisions by score:
- score >= 80 -> page oncall p0
- 50 <= score < 80 -> page p1 (team queue, with concise context)
- 30 <= score < 50 -> create incident ticket with automated context (no immediate page)
- score < 30 -> silent log event + attach to daily anomaly digest

Adaptive throttle policy (per-alert-group):
- window: 10m, threshold: 6 pages -> enter backoff
- backoff: 10m first, exponential up to 2h max while score band remains low (<50)
- backoff override: any p0-level SLO signal breaks the backoff immediately

Oncall triage checklist (minimal actionable steps):
1) Read synthesized context in page: score breakdown, top validators, recent sample plot link.
2) Check synth probes dashboard (if present) within 2m.
3) Inspect exporter scrape health (prometheus target scrape timestamps). If scrape gap found, annotate and mute noisy alerts for 15m with an automated note.
4) Correlate with downstream SLOs: run quick query for error_budget burn over last 1h. If burn > 25% of remaining budget -> escalate to incident.
5) If no corroboration and exporter healthy, escalate to infra oncall for deeper metric validity check (possible bad instrumentation push).
6) If widespread similar alerts across unrelated services -> suspect infra (prometheus, relay, retention) and call platform pager.

Runbook automation ideas (short list):
- When scrape_ok_ratio < 0.7 for a given exporter cluster, auto-create a "scrape-health" investigation ticket and add relevant runbooks links.
- Auto-annotate alerts with the last commit ID for metrics library and recent deploys to help triage release-induced regressions.
- Provide a one-click mute-with-ticket action for oncall UI that sets the adaptive throttle for that alert-group and attaches a ticket with checkboxes.

Experiment plan (MVP):
- Phase A (3 weeks): implement scoring proxy that ingests alert candidates from Alertmanager webhook and augments with validators (reads Prometheus, synth results). Do not alter paging — just log decisions and show proposed routing.
- Phase B (2 weeks): allow low-risk routing changes (create tickets instead of pages for score<50) for non-prod namespaces or a small service subset (billing, internal-config). Monitor missed real incidents.
- Phase C (rollout): add adaptive throttle and mute-with-ticket actions for teams that opt in.

Risks and open questions:
- Risk of suppressing real incidents that are noisy by nature (high-variability services). Mitigation: whitelist critical SLOs from suppression, and require synth corroboration.
- How to operationalize validator thresholds per-metric type (latency vs gauge vs counter)? Need a classification mapping and initial defaults per metric family.
- Prometheus query load: running cross-metric validators at alert time could spike Prometheus. Consider precomputing validator features (rolling windows) and caching scores.
- Auditability: must persist score+validators in alert history to avoid oncall surprise.

Immediate action items (owner in parens):
- Prototype scoring proxy skeleton and demo on test-alerts (Sofia).
- Draft PromQL validator set and run locally against 30d data (Ethan).
- Identify 3 candidate services for Phase A (Ravi + Maya) — prefer mid-criticality teams with responsive owners.
- Add a Confluence page summarizing decision criteria and the whitelist (Sofia).

Notes to self / messy bits:
- Keep the initial model simple and transparent. Oncall should see why an alert was demoted in a one-screen view.
- We want synthetic probes to be cheap and safe; consider a cached echo that avoids full model execution but still exercises the path.
- Consider a daily digest for teams listing all demoted alerts so owners can review false negatives.

Investigation sample (example timeline from last week):
- 2025-02-05 03:42 UTC: sudden burst of latency alerts for inference-gateway-prod (300 alerts in 12m).
- Sentinel analysis: scrape_ok_ratio for exporter-hostgroup-4 dropped to 0.6 for a 4m window; contiguous_samples for latency metric showed a 1-sample run. Synthetic probe remained green. Computed score median=28 -> recommended ticket.
- Action taken: automated throttle engaged; oncall created ticket; infra team found exporter process restarted due to OOM after recent rollout. Fix deployed at 04:10 UTC; alerts returned to baseline.
- Lesson: early mute prevented a 2-hour pager storm for an issue that didn't correspond to customer-impacting SLO burn. Good outcome.

Endnotes:
- This doc is intentionally informal and will be iterated. Please add notes inline or attach experimental telemetry dashboards for the validators.
- Next sync: SRE weekly sync, 2025-03-05, 10:00 PT — demo prototype if ready.
